output.brief: Android login success fell because of the vendor's edge rule update, not the 6.14 release. The 3 March rule pack added a rule (AUTO-LIB-17) that blocks requests from the networking library that every Android version uses, on the password path. The first blocks came at 10:41 UTC, minutes after the rule pack went live. Every app version failed at the same moment, and 6.14 was only 5% of attempts. Quick-unlock, iOS and web were unaffected. The blocked requests came from about 41,300 installs, and 92% of those had logged in successfully before, so these are real customers. They are not bots. OS patch level made no difference. I'm quite confident (about 90%). Next steps: ask Corvane to set that new rule to log-only on the mobile password path, keeping rate limits, lockout and other rules on. Then confirm in telemetry that password success recovers. Don't roll back 6.14, don't raise bot sensitivity, and don't remove blocked attempts from the KPI. Those would hide the problem or add more false blocks. Contact-centre call growth is plausibly linked, but fee notices also contributed.
